# Central question

The intervention transfers animal *identity* (the name) in every C=2 cell, but does not
transfer *bound attributes* (leg count, class membership): dog-legs answered "2" while
describing a dog (and text says a dog has four legs); dog-property named dog, said "Dogs
are mammals", but answered "No" to "is it a mammal"; ant-property named ant but answered
"No" to a yes-antennae question and then looped (r2=0.370).

One C=2 random-direction cell (legs-dog-RAND) shows the opposite dissociation: the digit
moved to the target correct value ("4") while the text kept spider identity. So digit
movement and identity movement are separable.

Ask specifically: does the attenuation subspace plausibly encode a name/concept pointer
WITHOUT attribute bindings, or does the C=2 reflection overshoot attribute coordinates? What
cheap test discriminates these?

# span-correction (span_corrected_delta) construction pseudocode
# Commit: batchwork shared-model-batch branch, demo.py operation == "span_corrected_delta".
# -- PI/[k3] to orient the scientist review

# Notation
#   h        live residual at the edited position (source prompt stream, layer 20), 1 x D
#   U        orthonormal projector basis (rank r=4), D x r
#   Δ        template attenuation delta = mean(dog|ant template residual - spider template
#            residual) in the U-span, projected and norm-matched; D-vector
#   C        strength (2.0 in the tested cells; 0.0 is the identity control)

# 1. Fit the projector from templates (offline, before decoding).
Δ = U (Uᵀ (μ_target - μ_spider))       # project template mean difference into the U-span
Δ = Δ * ‖μ_target - μ_spider‖ / ‖Δ‖     # norm-match to the raw mean-difference (match_component_norm)

# 2. Continuous steering (generation path, every decode step at the edited position).
source_basis = target_basis = U          # span_correction sets this
for each decode step at the edited position:
    span = U (Uᵀ h)                      # live source component in the U-span  (P h)
    patched = h + C (Δ - span)           # span_corrected_delta equation
    # in the U-span coordinates this is:  P h' = (1-C) P h + C Δ
    #   C=0  -> P h' = P h               (identity)
    #   C=1  -> P h' = Δ                 (full set to the template delta)
    #   C=2  -> P h' = 2Δ - P h          (reflection of P h about Δ  -> overshoot)
    replace hidden residual at the edited position with patched

# 3. Random control (matched-norm, span-correction random0_C2).
random_delta = randn_like(Δ); random_delta = random_delta * ‖Δ‖ / ‖random_delta‖
patched = h + C (random_delta - span)    # same reflection, different delta direction
